transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, honestly, what brings me in is that my body just feels totally out of my control lately. Like, a couple weeks ago, I was pacing around my apartment all night—just back and forth, back and forth—making these incredibly detailed notes for a supper club I was going to start. I had the whole menu planned out, down to this wild mushroom risotto that my grandmother used to make. She always said the secret was in the broth, you know? She used to simmer it for two days straight. But anyway, yeah, I was pacing everywhere. And now... I don't know, lately I'm just so slowed down. My sister was over yesterday and she said it took me forever just to get my shoes on to go outside. Which is weird because I usually wear these slip-on Vans, the checkerboard ones? I got them on sale at the mall last year when I was looking for a new blender.
During these periods of high energy or slowed-down mood, have you ever heard voices, seen things others don't, or had beliefs that others found unusual or hard to believe?

Voices? Um, no, I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, sometimes at work—I'm a waiter at this Italian place downtown—sometimes I think I hear the chef calling for food runners when he didn't, but that's just because the kitchen has really terrible acoustics. It's built like this long metal tunnel. My manager, Dave, he has this incredibly loud, booming voice anyway. He actually used to be a theater major, which makes total sense when you hear him project across the dining room. We talked about it a lot back when I was still taking classes at the community college. I was actually looking into taking a lighting design course for a while, but the lab fees were just completely ridiculous. Like, why do I have to pay an extra two hundred dollars just to learn how to plug in a stage light? It doesn't make any sense, they already have all the equipment. But, um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, seeing things. No, no invisible people or weird beliefs or anything. Just Dave yelling about table four.
You mentioned the high-energy pacing and the current slowed-down feeling—about how many days has this current stretch, where you've been experiencing both symptoms together, been going on?

Days? Um... I'm really not sure. I haven't been keeping track. I think... maybe it started feeling like this all at once around Tuesday? Because Tuesday is when we get the fresh seafood delivery at work. It's always a total disaster because the delivery guy, Frank, he parks his refrigerated truck at this incredibly weird angle in the alley. It blocks the dumpsters completely, every single time. And he always wants to talk about his fantasy football team while we're trying to check the inventory and make sure the mussels are still alive. 

I don't even watch football, honestly. I tried getting into it back when I was living in the dorms because my roommate, Kyle, he bought this massive flat-screen TV off Craigslist. It was like sixty inches, just took up the entire wall. We actually had to move our mini-fridge into the closet just to make it fit, which was probably a huge fire hazard in retrospect. The cord was stretched so tight across the room. But Kyle was just completely obsessed with the Patriots, so we had to watch every game. 

Anyway, um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, the days. Yeah, I don't know exactly how many days it's been going on. I haven't really been counting, it's all just kind of a blur right now.

Aside from these last couple of weeks, have you noticed this kind of up-and-down pattern—periods of high energy followed by periods of feeling slowed down—happening on and off for months or years before this?

Well, um, yeah, actually. It's been happening for a while now. Like, maybe four months? It all really started after I got fired from the restaurant. Which was completely unfair, by the way. I mean, they said I was "unreliable," but I only missed two shifts because my car wouldn't start. It's this ancient Honda Civic, the transmission is completely shot. I took it to this mechanic on 4th Street, right next to that amazing bakery that sells the huge cinnamon rolls. Have you ever been there? The frosting is just incredible, they make it from scratch every morning. I used to go there all the time before my shifts, just to grab a coffee and a pastry. The barista there, Sarah, she always remembered my order. She had this really cool tattoo of a hummingbird on her wrist. I actually thought about getting a tattoo for a while, maybe a compass or something, but I have this terrible fear of needles. When I was a kid, I had to get a blood draw and I actually passed out right in the chair. My mom was so freaked out, she bought me a huge Lego set afterward just to calm me down. It was the pirate ship one, with all the little cannons that actually fired these tiny plastic cannonballs. We spent the whole weekend putting it together on the living room floor. But, uh... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, the up-and-down stuff. It's been about four months, ever since I lost that job.
Right now, during this slowed-down period, are you also noticing things like your thoughts racing, needing much less sleep than usual, or feeling unusually energized at the same time?

Um, yeah, actually. Even though I feel so heavy and slow right now, my brain is just going a million miles an hour. Like, I'll be sitting there, barely able to move, but my mind is jumping from, like, new recipes I want to try, to designing a logo for this food truck idea I had, to figuring out how to pitch it to investors, to finding a commercial kitchen space to rent... it just goes so fast. And I can't sleep at all because every single idea just sets off three more ideas. 

Speaking of food trucks, there's this amazing taco truck that parks near my apartment on weekends. The guy who runs it, Hector, he makes his own salsa verde from scratch, and it is just unbelievable. He roasts the tomatillos right there in the truck. I actually asked him for the recipe once, but he said it was a family secret that his grandmother brought over from Oaxaca. Oaxaca sounds like such a beautiful place, honestly. I watched this documentary about it on Netflix a few weeks ago. They have this incredible artisan craft scene, especially these hand-carved wooden animals called alebrijes. They paint them in these crazy, vibrant neon colors. I actually looked up how much it would cost to fly down there, just to see them being made. The flights were surprisingly cheap if you don't mind a layover in Mexico City. But the layover was like twelve hours, which is just ridiculous. What are you even supposed to do in an airport for twelve hours? I guess I could read, but I always get distracted by the people-watching. Airports have the most interesting people. 

But, um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the racing thoughts and not sleeping. Yeah, my brain just won't shut off, even when my body feels like lead.
Has this combination of racing thoughts and physical slowness been severe enough to interfere with your ability to work, care for yourself, or manage daily responsibilities?

Yeah, it's... it's been really bad. I haven't been able to hold together work plans or even figure out my rent arrangements. My whole life is just completely falling apart. I couldn't even manage basic responsibilities, like, at all. My sister actually had to take me to the crisis clinic because I just couldn't get anything organized on my own. 

My sister, she's usually so busy, you know? She works at this high-end real estate firm downtown. They sell these massive, multi-million dollar condos with floor-to-ceiling windows. I visited her office once, and the view was just insane. You could see all the way out to the harbor. There were these tiny little sailboats out on the water, they looked like little white triangles from that high up. I used to want to learn how to sail when I was younger. My grandpa had this old wooden boat he kept at a marina in Florida. We went down to visit him one summer, and it was so incredibly humid. Like, you step outside and just instantly start sweating. We went to this seafood place on the pier, and I had the best fried shrimp of my life. They served it in this little red plastic basket with checkered paper, and the cocktail sauce had this amazing kick to it, like real horseradish. I tried making cocktail sauce at home once, but I accidentally bought the wrong kind of horseradish. It was this weird, creamy sauce instead of the grated kind, and it totally ruined the flavor profile. I had to throw the whole batch out, which was a shame because I had already bought all these expensive tiger prawns from the market... 

Um, wait. What were you asking me? Oh, right. Yeah, the... the work stuff and taking care of myself. No, I haven't been able to do any of that. My sister had to step in and take me to the clinic because I just couldn't handle it.

Right now, during this mix of racing thoughts and physical slowness, are you experiencing any unusual beliefs—like having special abilities or being targeted by others—or sensing things that other people don't seem to notice?

No, I don't think so. I mean, my thoughts are going crazy, but I don't feel like I have superpowers or anything. And I'm not seeing things that aren't there. It's just my own brain driving me nuts. 

Speaking of driving, my sister actually drove me here today in her new SUV. It's one of those hybrid ones, super quiet. You can't even tell when the engine turns on. She got it in this really nice metallic blue color. Reminds me of this guitar I almost bought a few years ago. It was a Fender Stratocaster, same exact shade of blue, with a white pickguard. I used to play a lot in high school, mostly just messing around in my friend Dave's garage. Dave was an amazing drummer. He could play all these complicated Rush songs perfectly. His parents were so cool about us making noise, probably because his dad used to be in a cover band in the 80s. They mostly played Journey and Foreigner, that kind of stuff. I actually found one of their old cassette tapes in a box in Dave's basement once. Cassettes are making a comeback, you know. I saw a whole display of them at Urban Outfitters last week. They had the Guardians of the Galaxy soundtrack on tape, which is pretty funny when you think about it, since it's a movie from the future but it's all about old music... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the unusual beliefs and stuff. No, nothing like that. Just the racing thoughts.

She got it in this really nice metallic blue color. Reminds me of this guitar I almost bought a few years ago. It was a Fender Stratocaster, same exact shade of blue, with a white pickguard. I used to play a lot in high school, mostly just messing around in my friend Dave's garage. Dave was an amazing drummer. He could play all these complicated Rush songs perfectly. His parents were so cool about us making noise, probably because his dad used to be in a cover band in the 80s. They mostly played Journey and Foreigner, that kind of stuff. I actually found one of their old cassette tapes in a box in Dave's basement once. Cassettes are making a comeback, you know. I saw a whole display of them at Urban Outfitters last week. They had the Guardians of the Galaxy soundtrack on tape, which is pretty funny when you think about it, since it's a movie from the future but it's all about old music... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the unusual beliefs and stuff. No, nothing like that. Just the racing thoughts.

Clear concurrent manic (racing thoughts, decreased sleep, flight of ideas) and depressive (psychomotor slowing, functional collapse) symptoms confirm a mixed episode rather than a purely depressive one (F31.4), supporting F31.60 as the best fit.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient describes a manic episode (decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, pressured/racing thoughts, grandiose entrepreneurial plans, flight of ideas with marked distractibility/tangentiality) occurring simultaneously with depressive/psychomotor slowing (psychomotor retardation, difficulty with basic self-care tasks like putting on shoes) within the same period—meeting criteria for a mixed episode. No hallucinations, delusions, or other psychotic features were endorsed despite specific probing, ruling out psychotic features or a primary psychotic disorder. History indicates a mood cycling pattern over ~4 months, consistent with Bipolar I Disorder, current episode mixed, without psychotic features.
